children.text: PREAMBLE

These Terms of Service constitute a legal agreement governing access to and use of the website operated by Youth Organization Union (Y.O.U) at https://youthorgunion.com/, together with the membership functions, organizational profiles, project submission functions, communication channels, digital resources, and other online services made available by or through Y.O.U

Youth Organization Union (Y.O.U) is a youth-led global network that brings together youth-led organizations across continents to promote sustainable development, global diplomacy, and meaningful social change. Y.O.U seeks to build connections across borders, cultures, and generations and to strengthen the capacity and collective voice of young people and youth organizations.

Y.O.U is operated on a non-distribution basis. The founding group holds 0% equity ownership in Y.O.U. It does not acquire any ownership interest in the organization's assets, revenues, intellectual property, or other property by virtue of its founding role. No profits or organizational surplus are distributed to founders or members as a return on ownership. Any revenue or surplus generated through Y.O.U’s activities is applied toward the organization’s purposes and operations in accordance with its governing documents and applicable law.

Y.O.U’s organizational identity is guided by its published Vision and Mission, together with the slogan “Where Unity Drives Change.”. The Vision and Mission published through Y.O.U’s official website form part of the organizational context within which the Service is provided.

The Service is a digital platform and communication environment of Y.O.U. It does not, solely by virtue of a person’s access to or participation in the Service, create any ownership interest, employment relationship, agency relationship, partnership, joint venture, or authority to legally bind Y.O.U except where Y.O.U expressly establishes such status or authority through Charter, Governance Policy, Membership Agreement, or another authorized written instrument.

C. Legal capacity and representative authority

Direct Members: the Continental Directors and Deputy Continental Directors serving within the continental structures of Africa, America, Asia, Australia and Europe. Subject to the Charter, the Governance Policy, the Membership Documents, Direct Members may represent their continental structures, participate in Union-level discussions and decision-making, leading activities within their assigned continents.

Indirect Members: Youth Leaders, Organization Members at continental level, and Country-Specific Sub-Members (collectively General Members). They participate within the relevant continental structures, engage through designated regional communication
channels (including regional messaging groups), and contribute to programs, initiatives, projects and collaborations.
The detailed rights, responsibilities, admission requirements and conditions of each category are governed by the Membership Agreement, the Charter and the Governance Policy.

Additional policies, guidelines, procedures, schedules, attachments, or terms applicable to a particular Service, program, membership category, or transaction may also be incorporated by reference and shall constitute “Additional Terms.”
Each Supplemental Term and Additional Term applies in the version duly adopted, published, or otherwise made applicable by Y.O.U from time to time, including subsequent amendments and revisions.
E. Order of Precedence

In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between these Terms and an applicable Supplemental Term or Additional Term, the following order of precedence shall apply, subject to mandatory applicable law:
(a) Y.O.U Charter; (b) Governance Policy; (c) Additional Terms; (d) Supplemental Terms; (e) General Terms of Service.
The Y.O.U Charter shall prevail with respect to the organization’s constitutional structure, governing bodies, offices, powers, and fundamental governance arrangements.
The Governance Policy shall prevail with respect to operational governance and decision-making matters falling within its scope.

Where an Additional Term specifically applies to a particular feature, program, service, or transaction, that Additional Term shall prevail over the Supplemental Terms and General Terms only to the extent of the relevant subject matter.
Supplemental Terms, including HR-, project-, membership-, donation-, or program-specific terms, shall prevail over the General Terms only with respect to the subject matter they specifically govern.
These General Terms shall serve as the baseline framework across the Platform but shall yield to the specialized documents above in their respective areas of governance.
RIGHTS & SCOPE LIMITATIONS
A. Rights of Members
Subject to these Terms and applicable Y.O.U. policies, members may use the portions of the Service made available to them for purposes connected with their Y.O.U participation.
Where the relevant functionality is available, members may:

(a) Maintain their organization’s profile; (b) Provide and update organizational information; (c) Submit, edit, and manage their own articles, events, and news; (d) Contribute information relating to programs and collaborations.
Otherwise use designated digital spaces made available to their membership category.

These rights are limited rights to use and manage content through the Service. They do not constitute ownership of the Service, website, platform infrastructure, database, domain name, Y.O.U brand, governance structure, or other property belonging to or controlled by Y.O.U
B. Organizational Property and Finance
Membership and participation do not create any right, title, or interest in Y.O.U’s:
(a) Funds or revenue; (b) Bank accounts; (c) Physical or digital assets; (d) Domains, websites, or platform infrastructure;
(e) Intellectual property; (f) Donor or partnership funds; (g) Other organizational properties.

Members may not independently control, allocate, transfer, commit, or otherwise dispose of Y.O.U funds or property unless such authority is expressly granted under the Governance Policy, Charter, or other applicable authorization.

Where the Revenue Allocation Principle (collectively RAP) is established by the applicable Governance Policy, revenue generated from partnership projects shall be allocated to Y.O.U’s designated operational budgets, including relevant personnel and implementation costs, rather than distributed to founders or members as ownership profits.
Nothing in these Terms should be interpreted as granting a member a personal entitlement to organizational revenue or assets.
C. Governance Bodies and Reserved Powers
Members may participate in Y.O.U’s discussions, programs, initiatives, consultations, and decision-making processes to the extent provided by the Charter, Governance Policy, and Membership Agreement.
Members shall not:
(a) Exercise powers reserved to Y.O.U’s governing bodies; (b) Interfere with the lawful authority of the Board, Directors, President, or other
designated officers; (c) Purport to exercise a governance power that has not been granted to them; (d) Bypass procedures or voting requirements established by the Charter or
Governance Policy or; (e) Make a decision on behalf of Y.O.U where the applicable governing document
reserves that decision to another body or officer.

Where the Governance Policy requires an approval threshold from the Board of Directors, specifically requiring agreement from at least two out of three (2/3) members that voting threshold shall strictly govern the matter. Such threshold may not be superseded, waived, or altered through informal communications, unilateral decisions, or arrangements outside the formal governance procedures established therein.
D. No Unauthorized Representation or Endorsement
A member may accurately identify itself as a member, a participant, or a partner of Y.O.U where such status exists.

A member must not, however, represent or imply that it is an official spokesperson of Y.O.U, is authorized to make official institutional statements on behalf of Y.O.U, has authority to agree or otherwise legally bind Y.O.U, has obtained Y.O.U’s endorsement, sponsorship, approval, or authorization where no such authorization exists, speaks on behalf of Y.O.U on an institutional position merely because of its membership or participation.
Official statements made on behalf of Y.O.U may be issued only by persons or offices expressly authorized to do so under the Y.O.U Charter, Governance Policy, or other applicable governing documents.
Membership, participation in a continental structure, or appointment to a regional or organizational role does not, by itself, constitute authority to speak officially on behalf of Y.O.U

Any permitted reference to the Y.O.U name, logo, slogan, or other branding assets must strictly comply with applicable Community & Content Guidelines and must not create any misleading impression of official affiliation, endorsement, sponsorship, or institutional sponsorship.

Any unauthorized representation, false implication of endorsement, or misuse of Y.O.U’s brand constitutes a material breach of these Terms and a serious violation of organizational standards. Pursuant to the Charter and Governance Policy, such conduct shall grant the Board of Directors the immediate authority to revoke membership, suspend portal access, and execute removal or termination without prior notice.

Member Content includes organizational profiles, research articles, project proposals, initiative descriptions, project materials, photographs and graphics, news and publications, educational or training materials and other original materials contributed by members.

STANDARDS OF CONDUCT & SAFEGUARDING

Every member organization, continental representative, youth leader, and individual user accessing or interacting with Y.O.U’s digital platforms agrees to be strictly bound by our safeguarding and ethical standards. Y.O.U enforces a policy of zero tolerance toward any form of abuse, harassment, exploitation, discrimination, or unlawful conduct across all digital and operational environments.
Y.O.U strictly prohibits any form of misconduct across all operations and platforms. Specifically, users and member organizations must comply with the following mandatory prohibitions:
A. Child Protection & Youth Safeguarding
(a) Under 13: Strict data privacy. Personal information may not be collected or
utilized absent parental approval. Automated restrictions are enforced on accounts that are not authorized; (b) Under 16: Strict content filtering. Complete ban on graphic violence, self-harm
content, gambling, and addictive algorithms built to take advantage of minors; (c) Under 18: Zero tolerance for adult or illegal content. Absolute ban on child sexual
abuse material (collectively CSAM), human trafficking, and marketing tied to alcohol, smoking, or commercial adult services.
B. Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI)
(a) Under 16: No heavy/hazardous child labor, no early or child marriage; (b) Under 18: No gender-based violence, sexual abuse, or commercial exploitation no
overnight or overtime shifts in restricted jobs; (c) Older Persons (60+): No ageist layoffs or hiring discrimination, no abandonment
or neglect of elders; (d) Workplace Equality: No different retirement ages or promotion barriers based on
gender, zero tolerance for sexual harassment; (e) Health: No gender-biased sex selection.
C. Preventing Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment (PSEAH)
(a) Child sexual abuse: Any sexual act involving someone under the age of 18
(regardless of consent or local laws); (b) Transactional sex: The exchange of money, employment, goods, services, or aid
benefits for sexual relations or sexual favors; (c) Abuse of power: Sexual relations between aid/support personnel and beneficiaries
that are based on an imbalance of status or power;
(d) Workplace harassment: Verbal, non-verbal, or physical conduct of a sexual nature
that is offensive, humiliating, or threatening, or that fosters a hostile work environment.
D. Digital Safeguarding & Online Ethics
(a) Under 13: Strictly banned from creating accounts. Parents must register and
manage services for them; (b) Ages 13–15: Allowed via Introductory Accounts with parental consent; (c) Ages 16+: Allowed independent accounts, subject to Strict Age Verification
(biometrics/ID) to stop age fraud; (d) Exploitation & Abuse: Any form of Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) or
explicit content that involves minors; (e) Cyberbullying: Harassment aimed at specific individuals, doxxing, defamation, or
identity theft (f) Dangerous Content: Self-harm, suicide encouragement, violence, hate speech, or
harmful viral challenges; (g) Illegal Advertising: Promoting alcohol, vapes, or gambling to minors.
E. Financial Integrity & Anti-Exploitation
(a) Under 13: Completely banned from all digital financial services, crypto wallets,
and in-game purchases; (b) Ages 13–15: Limited use of debit cards or digital wallets is allowed only when
linked to a parent's primary account, with strict spending caps and real-time parent alerts; (c) Under 18: Entirely prohibited from high-risk financial activities, including
cryptocurrency trading, margin trading, stock market investing, and gambling platforms.

This Privacy Policy will help you understand how the Youth Organization Union (Y.O.U) collects, uses, and protects the data you provide to us when you visit and use https://youthorgunion.com/.

When you access our website, register for membership, join our communities, you trust us with your data and we are fully committed to safeguarding your privacy in accordance with high standards of data security.

We reserve the right to change this policy at any given time, of which you will be promptly updated. If you want to make sure that you are up to date with the latest changes, we advise you to frequently visit this page.
COLLECTION OF DATA
We only collect personal information that is essential for running our operations and coordinating community activities. When you visit our website, we may collect the following data:
1. Personal Data (Information you voluntarily provide to us):

- Full name; - Official position or role within your organization; - Contact email address; - Phone number (personal or organizational representative); - Profile portrait photograph and personal social media links.
2. Automatic Data
- Your IP address; - Browser type, operating system, and device details; - Date and time of visit, pages viewed, and referring URLs.
WAYS TO COLLECT DATA
We collect personal data through your direct interactions with Y.O.U and automated website processes, including when you:
- Visit our official website: https://youthorgunion.com/;

- Subscribe to our newsletters, press releases, impact reports, or event updates; - Make a financial donation to support our programs and initiatives; - Submit an application form to become a member NGO or an official union; - Join official Y.O.U community groups on platforms; - Voluntarily complete surveys, provide feedback, or sign up for collective initiatives; - Use or view our website via your browser's cookies.
DATA USAGE
We use your personal data strictly to support our community operations and improve your experience with Y.O.U, including:
1. Member Verification & Management
Confirming your membership status, keeping our organization directory updated, and coordinating projects across regional chapters.
2. Communications & Updates
Sending news, impact reports, event invitations, and official policy updates.
3. Donation Processing
Safely handling donation transactions, issuing receipts, and tracking financial contributions for our action programs.
4. Surveys & Community Initiatives
Reviewing feedback and survey responses to improve our activities, campaigns, and youth initiatives.
5. Website Maintenance & Security
Analyzing basic technical data (like IP addresses and browser types) to keep our website secure, prevent spam, and improve site performance.
6. Third-party integrations
To run our operations smoothly, specialized technology partners process specific data on our behalf:
- Payment Gateways (e.g., PayPal): Securely handle payment details for your donations.

- Community Platforms (WhatsApp): Process your phone number and profile info when you join our online community groups, following Meta's privacy policies; - Email & Marketing Systems (Stripo, Mailchimp): Store your name and email address to send you regular newsletters and annual reports; - Content Management System (Strapi): Securely host internal databases and manage display profiles for member organizations.
DATA SHARING & PUBLIC DISCLOSURE

We strictly safeguard your privacy and never publicly disclose your personal information, except when necessary to foster transparent collaboration, verify official representation, and facilitate networking across our global youth movement. Personal data is only published when you voluntarily register for a public role within the organization or actively request public information, as outlined below:
1. General Visitors
No personal data is ever publicly disclosed when you browse our website.
2. Organizational Membership

General organizational profile details (organization name, logo, capability profile, and core activities) submitted via the Membership Registration Form are published on our website by default. For personal data, only the Contact Person’s information (full name, official email address, and representative phone number) is displayed publicly on the website directory. In the case the Head of Organization also serves as the Contact Person, their information details will be displayed similarly. All other Personally Identifiable Information (PII) remains strictly internal.
3. Youth Leaders

Public information on our main website is strictly limited to your portrait photograph, full name, official union position, and links to personal social media profiles (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn). All other personal data is kept internal and is only disclosed with the explicit consent of the Youth leaders.
4. Donors
Your identity and transaction details remain completely security and hidden (displayed as Anonymous) unless you actively option in or request to be acknowledged on our public donor list.
5. Online Community Groups (WhatsApp Platforms)

When you join official Y.O.U WhatsApp groups (e.g., Y.O.U GLOBAL or Continental Groups), your phone number and profile name will be visible to other group members to facilitate communication. Members are strictly prohibited from scraping, extracting, or misusing this data for personal or commercial gain.
DATA STORAGE

- Your data is not published in any form without permission from you, other than what you agree to make public when you register, as described in Data Sharing & Public Disclosure above; - We do not use your data for commercial purposes, and we do not sell, rent, or transfer it to any third party for profit.
DATA RETENTION

- Members and Youth Leaders: Data is stored throughout the duration of your valid membership in the alliance; - Donors: Transaction records are kept securely for one (01) year after your last transaction, for financial reconciliation and accounting; - Newsletter subscribers: until you unsubscribe; - Online community groups: while you remain in the group.
USER RIGHTS

- You have the right to access, check, request correction of, or request permanent deletion of your personal information from Y.O.U's systems; - You may unsubscribe from newsletters and notification emails at any time by following the instructions in our Community & Content Guidelines, or by using the "unsubscribe" link in any email; - To update, correct, or remove your information, please contact us directly at youthorgunion@gmail.com.
DATA SECURITY

We apply technical measures and management procedures to protect your data, and we commit to securely deleting personal data once we receive a valid request from you. If a data breach is likely to affect you, we will notify you and the relevant authorities as the law requires.

However, please note that no method of transmission over the Internet and no method of electronic storage is 100% secure. We do our best to protect your data, but we cannot guarantee absolute security against events beyond our control.
DONATION SECURITY & REFUND POLICY

A confirmation note of receipt is sent automatically to your email within twenty-four (24) hours after your donation is completed. Donors have the right to ask to cancel a donation and receive a refund within twenty-four (24) hours of making it. Refunds are returned to the same payment method you used. Processing through banks and payment gateways may take up to forty-five (45) days.
THIRD-PARTY LINKS

Our website may contain links to other websites and applications. This Privacy Policy applies only to our official website and to the social media pages managed directly by Y.O.U (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn and YouTube).

We do not own or control other websites and accept no responsibility for their content or privacy policies. We encourage you to read the privacy policies of these third parties carefully before giving them any personal information.
CHILDREN & YOUNG PEOPLE

Because Y.O.U works with young people, we follow the age rules in our Terms of Service. Children under 13 may not create accounts, and we do not collect their personal information without a parent's or guardian's approval. Young people aged 13 to 15 may use introductory accounts only with parental consent. People aged 16 and over may hold independent accounts, subject to age verification. If you are a parent or guardian and believe your child has given us data without your permission, please contact us and we will delete it promptly.
CHANGES TO THIS PRIVACY POLICY & CONTACT
We may revise and update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will let you know by updating the "Last updated" date at the top of this page, and changes take effect when they are posted here.

For important changes, we will notify you by email and/or through a prominent notice in the Partnership section of our website or on the Member Portal, at least thirty (30) days before they take effect.
For any questions, complaints, comments, or suggestions about this Privacy Policy,
please contact us at: youthorgunion@gmail.com
